correctness.rationale: A test proposal is blocked only if two accepted different-colour precursors lie in its exclusion region. Exact Poisson two-point factorial expansion has \(O(s^3)\) rejection remainder, because a third event in the finite Minkowski-expanded region has probability \(O(s^3)\). The two precursors overlap with measure T(E), forcing two different colors under both protocols; outside this overlap, independent uniformly random coloring blocks with probability \(1/2\), whereas first-available priority does not block. Insertion integrates these rejection rates to cubic densities with \(O(t^4)\) remainders. For intervals \(T=3\sigma^2\); for disks \(T=\sigma^4(\pi^2-3\sqrt3\pi/4)\), independently checked by radial numerical quadrature. The saved source checker passed 12 assertions and the explicit three-event witness.

value.rationale: The model source uses alleged density equivalence of random and priority color assignment in a first-layer recursion and extends that approach from continuum rods to disks. The first nonzero rejection coefficient is therefore a directly motivated, quantitatively important physical observable. This result supplies a strict, fully evaluated density difference in both dimensions, plus its geometric overlap mechanism, not just a contrived alternative notation or finite toy counterexample. It provides a rigorous short-time calibration of an approximation underpinning channel occupancy and multilayer packing; no global theorem or later-time prediction is claimed.
